findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate by -datetime; every optimized request 500s
findings.body: The endpoint orders by `-datetime` but uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, whose `get_item_key` does `int(math.floor(getattr(item, self.key)))` on the `datetime` attribute — `math.floor()` on a `datetime` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`. Even if that were fixed, `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value, which `build_queryset` then compares against a datetime column (`col <= %s` with a float), producing a database error. Unlike `DateTimePaginator` it has no strftime/multiplier conversion, so any request with `optimized_pagination=true` from a superuser/global-access member will return HTTP 500. The new paginator is unusable for this endpoint.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing crashes: Django does not support negative indexing
findings.body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[cursor.offset:stop]` with a negative start. The comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', but Django's QuerySet explicitly raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` for a negative slice start. Since cursor offsets are user-controlled via the cursor query parameter (`Cursor.from_string` happily parses `0:-5:0`), any admin hitting the audit log endpoint with such a cursor and `optimized_pagination=true` gets a 500. The 'advanced feature' is broken as implemented and the comment is factually wrong.

findings.title: SET→ZSET migration breaks in-flight buffered segments with WRONGTYPE errors
findings.body: The script and the Python producer switch segment buffer keys from Redis SETs (`sadd`/`scard`/`sunionstore`) to sorted sets (`zadd`/`zcard`/`zunionstore`), but existing keys in Redis written by the old code are still SETs. Calling `zcard`/`zunionstore` on a SET key (and likewise `p.zadd` in `SpansBuffer.process_spans`) raises a WRONGTYPE error, which aborts the Lua script and fails the whole batch of `EVALSHA` calls. During a rolling deploy — and for up to `redis_ttl` afterwards — all traces with segments buffered by the old code will cause consumer errors and those spans will not be buffered. There is no type check or migration path (e.g., probing with `type`/`object encoding`, or a key version bump).

findings.title: Hardcoded 1000-span eviction ignores max_segment_spans and silently drops spans
findings.body: The new eviction `if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)` hardcodes 1000, while `SpansBuffer` still accepts a configurable `max_segment_spans` (default 1001) that is now never used — the Python-side check that dropped oversized segments with a `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric and error log was removed from `_load_segment_data`. Consequences: (1) the configured limit is silently ignored, (2) spans are evicted silently instead of the segment being dropped with an error, so downstream consumers receive incomplete segments presented as complete, and (3) `zpopmin` evicts the lowest-scored (earliest `end_timestamp_precise`) spans, which can include the segment's root span, changing flush semantics. `max_segment_spans` should either be passed into the script or removed.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None, causing AttributeError for org-token auth
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `organization_context.member` unconditionally for non-superusers. For requests authenticated with an organization auth token (or any non-member context), `organization_context.member` is `None`, so this raises `AttributeError` and returns 500. Previously the audit log endpoint worked for any caller passing `OrganizationAuditPermission`. The member check needs a `None` guard.

findings.title: Redirect-follow limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without rationale
findings.body: The redirect-chasing loop was lowered from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000`, and the old comment documenting the consequence ('segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly') was deleted. Segment trees whose redirect chain exceeds 1000 hops will now silently stop being merged — children will stay in a separate set and be flushed as their own (incomplete) segment. If the reduction is intentional for latency, the trade-off should at least be documented; otherwise deep traces lose spans relative to the old behavior.

findings.title: KeyError on payloads missing end_timestamp_precise crashes the batch
findings.body: `Span(..., end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"], ...)` is a new hard dictionary access. The consumer only `cast`s the decoded JSON to `SpanEvent` and performs no schema validation, so any message lacking this field (older Relay payloads, malformed messages, spillover replays) raises `KeyError`, which fails the entire batch and causes it to be reprocessed in a crash loop. Previously this field was never read. Use `val.get(...)` with a fallback (e.g., 0 or the batch timestamp) if the field is not guaranteed to be present.
